source.author: C. Schoch
source.title: The Arcus Visionis of the Planets in the Babylonian Observations
source.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
source.provenance: NASA Astrophysics Data System scan of original RAS publication
source.inspection: Original scanned page-images visually checked on printed pp.732 and 734; text read on pp.731-734. No local raw-PDF byte SHA or calibration metadata attested.

original_observation_input.material: Historical Babylonian *planetary* observational date accounts published by Epping/Kugler and re-computed in 1924, NOT 70 first-naked-eye star events measured by Schoch

method.arcus_visionis_definition: Sun depression at the instant the star/planet sets on LAST visible evening or rises on FIRST visible morning (heliacal phases), in the author's assumed geometries
method.phase_labels: elast=evening LAST; mfirst=morning FIRST; for inner planets efirst=first evening appearance after solar conjunction is a distinct event class, not within-evening first noticing time.
method.applicability: Clear sky e.g. historical Babylon/Athens, stars near ecliptic with Sun-star azimuthal difference A <=25 degrees in recommendation.

reason: Listed late-depression values are Schoch recommendations, not timestamped direct visual sightings of individual stars.
Heliacal evening LAST / morning FIRST are different estimands from onset of naked-eye visibility of a star during ordinary evening twilight.
No star-by-star last NOT_SEEN to first confirmed SEEN with UTC timestamps, exact pointing and site, cloud/aerosol metadata, and adaptation/protocol.
Historical astronomy values and published outcomes cannot become newly result-blind held-out empirical validation.

forward_action: Continue existing authorized outreach and prospectively preregister consenting unaided-eye observers with last-NO/first-YES intervals, directional pointing plus measured cloud/AOD/adaptation, fixed candidate/model SHA and sealed predictions before observing. Preserve Taylor/Ann Arbor and Jerusalem holdouts and #60 safety controls.
